title: Byggentreprise OB2 - Møllebakken og Brevik pumpestasjoner
description: Denne anskaffelsen, OB2 – Byggentreprise for Brevik og Møllebakken pumpestasjoner er én av flere planlagte entrepriser i del-prosjektet «Overføringsanlegget», og er en utførelsesentreprise etter NS8405. Den gjelder hovedsakelig bygningsarbeidene i forbindelse med etablering av ny Brevik pumpestasjon og rehabilitering Møllebakken pumpestasjon. Følgende arbeider omfattes av Entreprise OB2 – Bygg og tekniske fag: Brevik pumpestasjon (nybygg): - Grunn- og betongarbeider - Bygningsmessige arbeider over og under terreng - Innvendige arbeider og tekniske rom - VVS- installasjoner tilknyttet bygget - Utomhusarbeider, inkludert terrengbearbeiding og landskapsutforming - VA-arbeider i tilknytning til pumpestasjonen - Midlertidig arbeider, rigg og drift Møllenbakken pumpestasjon (rehabilitering): - Rehabilitering og oppgradering av eksisterende bygningsmasse (mindre omfang) - Byggtekniske arbeider innvendig og utvendig - Etablering av nye VVS-installasjoner i bygget - Tilpasninger for nytt maskinteknisk og teknisk utstyr Det henvises for øvrig til vedlagte Teknisk beskrivelse, tegninger og øvrige dokumenter vedlagt konkurransegrunnlaget.

buyer: ЦЕНТЪР ЗА СПЕШНА МЕДИЦИНСКА ПОМОЩ - ВАРНА
title: Bulgaria – Medical consumables – ДИНАМИЧНА СИСТЕМА ЗА ПОКУПКИ (ДСП) ЗА ДОСТАВКА НА МЕДИЦИНСКИ ИЗДЕЛИЯ ЗА НУЖДИТЕ НА ЦСМП-ВАРНА
description: Динамичната система за покупки (ДСП) е изцяло електронен процес, който възложителите могат да използват при често осъществявани поръчки, чиито типови характеристики отговарят на изискванията на възложителите. Настоящата динамична система за покупки има за предмет доставката на медицински изделия за Центъра за спешна медицинска помощ – Варна (ЦСМП-Варна). Срокът за действие на настоящата ДСП е 36 (тридесет и шест) месеца. Прогнозната стойност е 206938,80 (двеста и шест хиляди деветстотин тридесет и осем лева и осемдесет стотинки) лева без ДДС. Динамичната система за покупки е отворена през целия срок на действие за всеки кандидат, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Достъпът и участието в нея са свободни и безплатни за всички заинтересовани лица. Настоящата динамична система за покупки не е обособена по отделни категории. В документацията са посочени около прогнозни 109 номенклатури с количества. Те са прогнозни с оглед на планираните нужди на възложителя. Възложителят не е обвързан от посочените количества, а ще поръчва с оглед конкретните си нужди по време на договора – прогнозните количества може да бъдат надхвърлени или да бъде поръчана по-малка бройка. Формите/разфасовките и артикулите са посочени с оглед реалната дейност на медицинския персонал в ЦСМП–Варна и окомплектоването на медицинските чанти. Първоначално планираната "Техническа спецификация" може да бъде частично променяна в хода на действие на динамичната система или в рамките на възлагане на конкретна поръчка по нея, като се добавят нови медицински изделия и/или се променят количествата им, както и като се променят изискванията към тях. Това може да стане и с документите към всяка конкретна обществена поръчка, възлагана в рамките на ДСП. Фактическото изпълнение на обществената поръчка ще се определи на базата на реално доставените медицински изделия, в рамките на финансовия ресурс.

title: Magneettikuvantamispalvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena on magneettikuvantamispalveluiden tuottaminen HUS Diagnostiikkakeskukselle Uudenmaan, Kymenlaakson ja Etelä-Karjalan alueille. Hankittava palvelu sisältää kaksi palvelukokonaisuutta 1) kiinteä magneettikuvantamispalvelu, joka tuotetaan Palveluntuottajan toimitiloissa ja resursseilla kiinteästi sijoitetulla magneettilaitteella ja 2) liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu (ns. magneettivaunu), joka tuotetaan Tilaajan toimitilojen yhteydessä. Palvelukokonaisuudet on jaettu maantieteellisiin osa-alueisiin. Palveluntuottaja voi tarjota vain toiseen tai molempiin palvelukokonaisuuksiin. Kiinteän magneettikuvantamispalvelun osalta Palveluntuottaja voi tarjota palvelua yhdelle tai useammalle maantieteelliselle alueelle. Liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu käsittää koko HUS Diagnostiikkakeskuksen toiminta-alueen. Siis, mikäli palveluntuottaja osallistuu liikuteltavan magneettikuvantamispalvelun tuottamiseen, on sen tarjottava kaikkiin liikuteltavan magneettikuvantamispalvelun osa-alueisiin (osa-alueet 4–7)., Kiinteä magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Uudenmaan alue Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Kiinteä magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Kymenlaakson alue Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Kiinteä magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Etelä-Karjalan alue Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Pääkaupunkiseutu (Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa) Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Kymenlaakson alue Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Etelä-Karjalan alue Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., Liikuteltava magneettikuvantamispalvelu, Lohja, Hyvinkää, Porvoo ja Raasepori Palvelu on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 2 (Palvelukuvaus)., TYHJÄ LUOKKA (ÄLÄ TÄYTÄ TÄHÄN) Tämä osa-alue jätetään tyhjäksi, ellei hankintayksiköllä ole tarvetta kesken dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän ottaa uutta osa-aluetta käyttöön.,

title: Environmental Science and Engineering Contract, A-E Services to be Ordered on Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity Schedule
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE HAS BEEN UPDATED, SEEKING SF330 SUBMITALS. THERE IS NO RFP PACKAGE TO DOWNLOAD. ALL INFORMATION NEEDED TO SUBMIT SF330 DOCUMENT IS CONTAINED HEREIN. SF 254S AND SF 255S WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. NOTE: FAR PART 12 (COMMERCIAL) IS NOT APPLICABLE TO THIS PROCUREMENT. SUMMARY: The Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC), Port Hueneme, California is soliciting SF330s for a single-award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Architect and Engineering (A-E) contract for various environmental restoration (ER) and other environmental projects. The A-E services required will include professional services to enable NAVFAC EXWC to support other NAVFAC commands, as well as other Department of War (DoW) and federal agencies. Market research was conducted in May 2026 and there were too few qualified small businesses to warrant consideration of a set-aside, therefore this acquisition is being issued under Full and Open Competition. The North American industry Classification System (NAICS) code is the procurement 541330, and the annual size standard is $25,500,000. NAVFAC EXWC anticipates the award of an IDIQ with base ordering period of sixty (60) months, and an extension of services period not to exceed six months. The maximum value of all task order placed under this contract will not exceed $150,000,000. Individual task orders under this contract may be firm fixed price (FFP) (Estimated 40%) or cost-plus-fixed fee (CPFF) (Estimated 60%). The minimum guarantee for the IDIQ contract is $10,000. Individual task orders are anticipated to range $5,000 to $6,000,000 per task order. The estimated award date is March 2027. PROJECT INFORMATION: Firms must be capable of performing work on a wide variety of projects in Environmental Restoration (ER) and other environmental topics, in a manner that complies with federal, state, and local regulations and laws, and within timeframes required. This work will support the A-E services that NAVFAC EXWC provides to support the environmental cleanup of sites managed by the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. Although, the majority of the work is expected to be in the continental United States, project sites could be worldwide. Specific needs will be determined based upon project requirements and as described in each task order�s Performance Work Statement or Statement of Work. A-E services required under this contract include, but are not limited to: - Environmental program development and implementation. Particularly, the contractor will support development and implementation of the Navy�s environmental restoration (ER) program, comprising the Installation Restoration (IR) and Munitions Response (MR) Programs in terms of the associated science and engineering, regulations, and policy - Research, development, testing, and evaluation (RDT&E) of innovative environmental technologies, techniques, and solutions, particularly for environmental restoration. - Planning and pilot-testing innovative environmental technologies, techniques, investigations, and solutions to support full-scale design. - Services for associated environmental programs, including remedy resilience, impacts of elevated sea water levels and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resources management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resources management. The services at ER sites may involve supporting NAVFAC EXWC in the preparation, expert review, or optimization of preliminary assessments, site inspections, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, engineering evaluation/analysis (EECA), proposed plans, records of decision (RODs), remedial designs, sampling and analysis plans (SAPs) or Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and five-year reviews for customers in the Department of the Navy and other federal agencies. These services may include site characterization, laboratory studies, and pilot testing with the aim of helping NAVFAC EXWC and its customers develop cost-effective full-scale designs and solutions for environmental projects. An important component of the services also is technology transfer (T2) to and training of the Department of the Navy and other federal agency personnel (and their contractors), who are engaged in ER or other environmental programs. Other environmental project areas may include (but are not limited to) remedy resilience, coastal flooding from seawater and groundwater, and extreme weather events, active range sustainability, sustainable water resource management, environmental compliance, energy efficiency, and natural resource management. For on-site investigations, firms must provide personnel with current health and safety training, as required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and adhere to all NAVFAC requirements for Health and Safety. Task orders will be issued with a project/site specific Scope of Work under the general scope of the contract. Typically, requests for proposals issued for individual task orders will include a general Scope of Work or a performance-based acquisition Performance Work Statement, location of work, character and extent of services required, technical requirements in addition to the requirements contained within Statement of Architect and Engineering Services (SAES). SELECTION CRITERIA: The selection criteria are listed below in descending order of importance. Items (1) thru (5) are primary criteria and (6) thru (7) are secondary criteria. Secondary criteria will only be used as 'tie-breakers' among technically equal firms. (1) Professional Qualifications: Professional Qualifications: The offeror shall provide no more than thirteen (13) resumes in Section E of the Standard Form (SF) 330. If more resumes are submitted than requested, then only the first thirteen will be considered. Providing less resumes is encouraged if provided personnel fulfill multiple roles. Experience that is not related to the work described in this solicitation should not be included. Resumes shall not be more than 2 pages each. Firms will be evaluated in terms of the general professional qualifications and technical competence in areas of work described in the "Project Information" section above. The evaluation of the resumes will consider education, training, registration, certifications, overall and relevant experience, and longevity with the firm. Projects that demonstrate successful optimization efforts that reduced project cost or time and added unique technical value, successful execution of projects where standards and methods for execution were not commonly accepted, or projects that had complex hydrogeological and regulatory site conditions will be given preference. Additionally, projects performed for the Navy or DoW as opposed to other federal agencies or other clients are preferred. Experience on the resumes should be within the last 8 years to be considered relevant. Resumes should be presented in the following three categories: Program Manager (PGM), Project Managers (PMs), and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) in the technical areas listed above. The PGM and PMs should have a degree in engineering (environmental, civil, chemical, or related), or geological sciences, professional registrations in at least one state of the United States, and at least five (5) years of experience in managing programs or projects of similar size and complexity as expected in this contract. The states of registration and certification of relevant personnel must be included on each resume in Section E of SF 330. One PGM resume and two (2) PM resumes are required.The resumes will be rated more favorably when they demonstrate specialized experience and technical competence in the following areas: � Investigation and/or remediation of environmental media contaminated with emerging contaminants, particularly PFAS, especially projects executed for the Navy or DoW; � Inve

Verträge, die im open-house-Modell geschlossen werden, unterfallen mangels Auswahlentscheidung nicht dem Vergaberecht. Eine Unterwerfung unter vergaberechtliche Regelungen ist mit der Verwendung dieses Formulars nicht verbunden. Die AOK Bayern beabsichtigt, mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen nicht-exklusive Rabattvereinbarungen über den Wirkstoff Relugolix, ATC L02BX04, nach § 130c Abs. 1 SGB V zu schließen. Die AOK Bayern bietet allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, die die unten genannten Eignungsvoraussetzungen erfüllen, den Abschluss identischer und nicht individuell verhandelbarer Rabattvereinbarungen an. Der frühestmögliche Vertragsbeginn ist der 01.01.2026, alle Verträge enden am 31.12.2027. Ein Vertragsschluss ist während dieser Laufzeit jederzeit möglich, spätestens jedoch am 03.11.2027. Die Verträge können mit einer Frist von einem Monat zum Monatsende gekündigt werden. Bei Inkrafttreten eines durch bundesweite oder landesspezifische, im offenen Verfahren geschlossenen Rabattvertrags über Arzneimittel mit dem auftragsgegenständlichen Wirkstoff treten die open-house-Vereinbarungen automatisch für die entsprechende Laufzeit außer Kraft. Ein Vertrag wird mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen geschlossen, die ihre Eignung durch eine ausgefüllte und unterschriebene Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit nachweisen. Der pharmazeutische Unternehmer hat den ausgefüllten und unterzeichneten (die Vertretungsberechtigung des/der Unterzeichner/s muss sich aus dem Handelsregisterauszug ergeben, anderenfalls ist eine Vollmacht vorzulegen) Vertrag nebst ausgefüllter und unterzeichneter Anlage "Festlegung der vertragsgegenständlichen Arzneimittel" sowie die ausgefüllte und unterzeichnete Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit einzureichen. Die Unterlagen können ENTWEDER in SCHRIFTFORM von Hand unterzeichnet ODER ELEKTRONISCH mit einer qualifizierten elektronischen Signatur eingereicht werden. Von Hand unterzeichnete Unterlagen in SCHRIFTFORM sind in 2-facher Fassung im Original an folgende Adresse einzusenden: AOK Bayern - Die Gesundheitskasse Vergabestelle SGB V ZE25 open-house Rabattverträge Carl-Wery-Str. 28 81739 München ELEKTRONISCHE Unterlagen mit einer qualifizierten elektronischen Signatur sind über den Kommunikationsbereich im Vergabeportal www.dtvp.de einzureichen. Bei Eingang vollständiger und korrekter Unterlagen bis zum 03. eines jeden Monats erfolgt der Vertragsbeginn zum darauf folgenden nächsten Monatsersten, ansonsten zum darauf folgenden übernächsten Monatsersten. Bei von Hand unterzeichneten Unterlagen in SCHRIFTFORM ist eine Übersendung der vollständigen, ausgefüllten und unterzeichneten Unterlagen vorab als Scan an die E-Mail-Adresse vergabestelle1@by.aok.de oder über den Kommunikationsbereich im Vergabeportal www.dtvp.de fristwahrend, wenn die vollständigen und korrekten Originalunterlagen in Papierform bis zum 10. des Monats bei der AOK Bayern, Vergabestelle, eingehen. Bitte beachten Sie die Ausfüllanleitung, die unter www.dtvp.de bei den Vergabeunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt wird. Interessierte pharmazeutische Unternehmen können im Projektraum zum Open-House-Verfahren auf dem Portal www.dtvp.de die Freischaltung der Vergabeunterlagen beantragen. Ein Link zum Portal befindet sich in dieser Bekanntmachung. Als potentielle Vertragspartner kommen ausschließlich pharmazeutische Unternehmen in Betracht. Die Unterlagen des Open-House-Verfahrens werden ausschließlich pharmazeutischen Unternehmen als potentiellen Vertragspartnern freigeschalten und sind streng vertraulich zu behandeln. Durch die Beantragung der Freischaltung durch die Unternehmen wird die vertrauliche Behandlung der Unterlagen bestätigt.

description: NOTICE OF SOLICITATION NUMBER CHANGEThe Bonneville Powerhouse II Unwatering Pump Replacement acquisition, previously announced under presolicitation notice number W9127N26BA018, is now identified as W9127N27BA012 due to the fiscal-year transition. This presolicitation notice continues the announcement of the same acquisition under the new number; it does not represent a separate requirement.All subsequent notices and solicitation documents for this acquisition will reference solicitation number W9127N27BA012.The original presolicitation notice under W9127N26BA018 is available here: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/dce799052d0043619ff7a08ccb237c50/view The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District (NWP) has a requirement for Unwatering Pump Replacement at the Bonneville Lock and Dam Powerhouse II. Contractor access to the work site will be from Interstate 84 on the Oregon side of the Columbia River via Exit 40, approximately four miles west of Cascade Locks, Oregon. All work for this project is in Skamania County, Washington. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC). This solicitation requires the contractor and or subcontractor(s) information system to process, store, or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI), and requires the contractor and or subcontractor(s) to comply with CMMC requirements. The CMMC level required by this solicitation is: CMMC Level 1 (Self). This CMMC level, or higher, is a condition of award. Prior to award, the apparent successful bidder must have a current CMMC status at Level 1 (Self), or higher, posted in SPRS for each relevant CMMC UID in order to remain eligible for award; failure to meet this requirement will render the bidder ineligible for contract award.CMMC requirements apply to prime contractors and subcontractors throughout the supply chain at all tiers that will process, store, or transmit any FCI on contractor information systems in the performance of this contract or subcontract. Prime contractors shall comply and shall require subcontractors to comply with and to flow down CMMC requirements, such that compliance will be required throughout the supply chain at all tiers with the applicable CMMC level and assessment type for each subcontract as follows:If a subcontractor will not process, store, or transmit FCI in performance of the subcontract, then no CMMC level is required for that subcontractor. If a subcontractor will only process, store, or transmit FCI in performance of the subcontract, then a CMMC status of Level 1 (Self) is required for that subcontractor.Prime contractors are responsible for ensuring that all covered subcontractors obtain and maintain the appropriate CMMC level and assessment type for the information they will process, store, or transmit during performance.For this solicitation, contractors requesting access to documents containing FCI must have an active SAM registration and a current NIST SP 800 171 assessment with at least a Basic confidence level recorded in SPRS.Summary of Work: Work includes but is not limited to providing all labor, equipment, and materials required to procure, install, and test one vertical turbine unwatering pump assembly per the Contract specifications. The Government will remove the existing pump. Procure and install one 7,000 gpm vertical turbine unwatering pump. Procure and install all the discharge head piping necessary to connect with existing discharge piping to the North pump assembly.Procure and install one 460V, 3 phase motor as detailed in the specifications.Test all equipment prior to commissioning and turning over to the Government.The anticipated completion date for physical construction is 180 calendar days after receiving the Notice to Proceed. The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This acquisition will result in a single firm-fixed-price contract.The estimated magnitude of construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Sources Sought Notice Notice Number: FA301627Q7005 Response Deadline: November 5, 2026, at 10:00 AM Central Time (CT) Primary NAICS Code: 238290 � Other Building Equipment Contractors (Elevator Installation, Modernization, and Repair) Alternative NAICS: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Product Service Code (PSC): J039 � Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Elevators Place of Performance: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, Building B663, 10257 East St W, Randolph AFB, TX 78150 2. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This is a Sources Sought Notice only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research to determine the availability, interest, and technical capabilities of qualified businesses to perform elevator modernization and environmental investigation services at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA), Texas. 3. PROJECT SCOPE & REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall provide all materials, labor, specialized technicians, and equipment necessary to complete the modernization and component replacement of the elevator at Building B663, Randolph AFB. The project requires specialized capabilities across two primary areas: A. Elevator Modernization & Mechanical Scope Full Replacement: Complete replacement of existing mechanical, control, and hydraulic components with non-proprietary, open-architecture equipment ensuring onboard diagnostics are accessible to any licensed elevator mechanic without proprietary software, factory passwords, or special tools. Compliance Standards: Ensure the entire system is fully compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), ASME A17.1-2016/CSA B44-16, and Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 754 (TAC Ch. 74). Licensing Requirement: All elevator-specific work must be executed by a Texas Licensed Elevator Contractor. Key Components to Install: New, double-bottom hydraulic jack with protective PVC liner. New door operator and electronic safety edges on the elevator car. New microprocessor-based, non-proprietary controller. New ADA-compliant car operating panels (COP), hall stations, and emergency two-way communication system. Energy-efficient equivalents of the pump unit, submersible motor, and control valves. Testing & Certification: Perform full-range operational and load tests, and certify the elevator upon project completion. B. Environmental Investigation & Remediation Scope Soil Testing: Execute borings to collect soil samples at various depths around the elevator hydraulic jack cylinder/pump jack casing to test for hydraulic fluid contamination (in accordance with EPA-approved procedures). Analytical Reporting: Deliver a comprehensive laboratory analysis report within 20 days of inspection detailing field activities, boring logs, mapping, and a determination of any leaks. Regulatory Compliance (TCEQ / TRRP): If no release is found under the Texas Risk Reduction Program (TRRP - 30 TAC 350) rules, prepare a report to support a Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) "No Further Action" (NFA) letter. If a release is detected, develop a detailed Remedial Action Plan (RAP) within the 30-day Period of Performance (PoP) for submission to TCEQ, Civil Engineering (CE), and Contracting (CONS). If required, perform environmental remediation (excavation, proper containerization/disposal of hydraulic fluid and contaminated soil, and clean backfill). 4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS & QUESTIONNAIRE Interested firms must submit a Capability Statement addressing the following areas: Section I: Corporate Profile 1. Company Name & Address 2. Unique Entity ID (UEI) & CAGE Code 3. Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email) 4. Socioeconomic Status (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, HUBZone, WOSB, Large) 5. Bonding Capacity (Single Project & Aggregate) Section II: Technical Experience & Capabilities Elevator Licensing: Confirm your firm's status (or your proposed subcontractor's status) as a registered Texas Licensed Elevator Contractor. Elevator Modernization Experience: Describe at least one (1) project completed within the past two (2) years demonstrating experience with the replacement of mechanical, control, and hydraulic systems using non-proprietary, open-architecture equipment. Environmental & Remediation Experience: Detail your capability to conduct soil borings, EPA-approved laboratory sampling for hydraulic fluid, and your team's familiarity with Texas Risk Reduction Program (TRRP - 30 TAC 350) rules and Remedial Action Plan (RAP) development for the TCEQ. Military/DoD Installation Experience: Describe your experience managing construction or maintenance projects on active military bases (specifically regarding secure access control, Entry Authority Lists [EAL], AT Level 1 Awareness Training, and coordination with Base Civil Engineering). 5. HOW TO RESPOND Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist (insert agency email addresses). Subject Line of Email: Response to Sources Sought: FA301627Q7005 - B663 Elevator Modernization Response Deadline: November 5, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT

title: AMARG Wastewater Treatement System and Service
description: The 355th Contracting Squadron intends to award a sole-source, Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to Evoqua Water Technologies LLC, CAGE 72XB4 located at 11147th St Pittsburgh, PA 15201. The anticipate award date is 18 November 2026 with an ordering period of 1 December 2026 � 30 November 2031 for an amount not expected to exceed $70,000.00. Point of Contact: Patricia Murray, Contracting Officer 355th Contracting Squadron 3180 S. Craycroft Rd B2528 Davis-Monthan AFB, AZ 85707 Email: patricia.murray.6@us.af.mil Commercial Phone: 520-228-3095 NAICS: 333310 PSC: W046 Description of Supplies/Services: The requirement includes continuous equipment rental, preventative maintenance (PM), and service of the installed Industrial Wastewater Treatment System supporting industrial operations of paint booths for the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group (AMARG). This current equipment is provided under a rental agreement and not Government Furnished Property. The proposed contract action will include continuous equipment rental, quarterly preventive maintenance, consumable filter replacements, resin tank exchange/regeneration, and certified hazardous waste transport is required to ensure uninterrupted mission readiness, personnel safety, and regulatory compliance. The contractor will provide all necessary personnel, supervision, tools, materials, and equipment required to perform preventative maintenance and repair services as identified in the PWS and IAW OEM equipment rental and servicing standards. Services include but are not limited to The scope of work includes the following tasks: Scheduled Maintenance: The contractor will perform on-site Preventive Maintenance (PM) actions on at least a quarterly basis or as needed based on system usage as specified by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM). This includes, at a minimum, verifying the calibration and proper operation of all differential pressure gauges, flow controllers, switches, and electronic sensors against Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications. Replace the system�s pre-filtration media, replace ion exchange tanks, and ensure proper disposal of all Hazardous Materials IAW all applicable waste handling and disposal regulations. System Diagnostics and Repair: The contractor will conduct a complete diagnostic inspection of the system and all components to identify the cause of any operational defects. The contractor will execute all necessary repairs to restore the system to its original performance specifications. This proposed Sole Source action will be awarded following the procedures at RFO 12.201-1(e)(3). The installed system is provided under a rental agreement, and all equipment remains the property of Evoqua Water Technologies LLC, the OEM. Evoqua has not identified any third-party authorized distributors or servicers of their equipment. Market research included internal Government sources and strategic sourcing vehicles; no suitable sources were identified. Price evaluations found the cost associated with removal of the current system and installation/commissioning of a new system are not reasonably expected to be recovered through competition over the anticipated ordering period. Additionally, such transition efforts have the potential to disrupt paint booth operations, which could result in additional costs to the Government. Based on these considerations, and the equipment ownership and servicing restrictions, the Contracting Officer has determined, as authorized at RFO 12.102(a), that only one source is reasonably available to provide continued rental and servicing of the installed system. Establishment of a Sole Source BPA with Evoqua Water Technologies, LLC represents the best value and is in the best interest of the Government. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties may provide a capability statement with clear and convincing evidence identifying their ability to support this requirement as identified. Such parties must respond by Friday, 6 November 2026 by 1:00PM MST to Contracting Officer Patricia Murray at email: patricia.murray.6@us.af.mil or phone (520) 228-3095. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed action based upon responses is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Pre-solicitation Notice: On-Ramp for the Department of Defense OMNIBUS IV Multiple-Award Contract
description: Amendment 0001 to this notice is to push out the anticipated posting of the solicitation to late November 2026. This is a pre-solicitation notice to synopsize the intention of the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for an on-ramp to the OMNIBUS IV Multiple Award, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle covering military medical research and development services. A historical pre-solicitation notice was posted under Notice ID# HT942626RE002, although there were various delays with getting a solicitation out in Fiscal Year 2026. This notice is taking over where Notice ID# HT942626RE002 left off. No further delays are anticipated at this time for this on-ramp. The eventual RFP will be set-aside for small businesses certified under the Small Business Administration 8(a) Program. The Government anticipates making multiple new awards under this on-ramp, and all new awards will align with the existing unrestricted contract vehicle. This notice is not a request for proposals and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. The OMNIBUS IV contract vehicle was awarded under full and open competition with a base ordering period of 20 June 2022 through 19 June 2027 and an Option Ordering Period of 20 June 2027 - 19 June 2032. Task orders may be competed under fair opportunity (providing all Contract Holders within a Market Segment the opportunity to submit a proposal) or an exception to fair opportunity (such as set-asides for small businesses or applicable small business socioeconomic categories). The cumulative ceiling of this unrestricted IDIQ contract vehicle is $10 billion. To date, the accumulated awarded task order value (including future unexercised option periods) is over $690 million across 61 task orders. Task Orders have been issued by a growing number of end users including DHACA, the U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (now integrated into DHACA), the Naval Supply Systems Command, and the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences. When excluding the task orders simply providing a minimum guarantee to the existing Contract Holders, 61 task orders have been issued off this contract vehicle with 8 task orders being set aside for the 8(a) Program and 15 task orders being awarded to an 8(a) Participant (based on the most recent representations at the contract level). 42 task orders have been awarded so far to small businesses under this contract vehicle. Of the 61 task orders, 95% were awarded during the Government Fiscal Years 2024 - 2026. Please see attachments for further details.

title: Commercial Solutions Opening for Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2)
description: Amendment 01 dated 12 July 2021: Updated "CSO" to read "Commercial Solutions Opening" in an effort to prevent confusion with other acronyms. Federal Agency: Air Force Program Office: AFLCMC/XA �Architecture and Integration Directorate� CSO Title: JADC2 Commercial Solutions Opening CSO Type: Commercial Solutions Opening with Calls CSO Number: FA8612-21-S-C001 CSO Date: June 28, 2021 NOTE This is only an announcement; PLEASE DO NOT SUBMIT PROPOSALS IN RESPONSE. Subsequent calls will be issued under this announcement to solicit proposals for specific efforts. Please refer to the attachment section of this announcement for the calls. Publication of this announcement does not obligate the DoD to review any white papers submission beyond an initial administrative review, or to award any specific project, or to obligate any available funds. 1.0 OVERVIEW This Commercial Solutions Opening is intended to be as streamlined as possible to allow the Architecture and Integration Directorate (AFLCMC/XA), or any organization AFLCMC/XA supports, to leverage the latest technology advances from a large variety of prospective Contractors. AFLCMC/XA invites innovative technical approach proposals addressing Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) problems associated with getting the right information to the right platform/decision maker in the most efficient manner thereby reducing kill chain and Observe, Orient, Decide and Act (OODA) timelines and cycles. This Commercial Solutions Opening will focus on existing and emerging technologies and platforms across the Defense Department, the Intelligence Community, and the commercial world, to perform an integrated analysis of the capability of various options to contribute to the fight and prioritize investments over time. This solicitation is not requesting any white papers or proposals at this time. This Commercial Solutions Opening functions as the overarching umbrella solicitation from which Calls will be published. This Commercial Solutions Opening will remain open for Calls until rescinded. This Commercial Solutions Opening can result in the award of FAR Part 12 Contracts, Procurement for experimental purposes under 10 U.S.C. 4023 or Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) under 10 USC 4021. Over the course of this time period, AFLCMC/XA will publish Calls via amendments to this Commercial Solutions Opening. These Calls will contain specific Areas of Interest (AoIs) related to JADC2�s Technology Focus Areas. Those specific AoIs are what prospective Contractors shall focus their solutions towards. This is a competitive solicitation that seeks to fund innovative technologies that propose new solutions to expand Air Force capabilities as it relates to JADC2 Technology Focus Areas. AFLCMC/XA is interested in receiving responses from all interested offerors to include, but not limited to, the following: traditional defense contractors, nontraditional defense contractors, large businesses, small businesses and research institutions. The Commercial Solutions Opening is a streamlined acquisition process that seeks to reduce acquisition timelines and acquire new, innovative solutions that companies can bring forth to meet the stated AoIs detailed in each Call. All details of the process shall be governed by this Commercial Solutions Opening unless otherwise noted or expanded upon in each Call. AFLCMC/XA is not obligated to make any awards as a result of this Commercial Solutions Opening and all awards are subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by the proposer prior to the issuance of any contract award. AFLCMC/XA reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this Commercial Solutions Opening and each subsequent Call. The Commercial Solutions Opening authority reference to Class Deviation 2022-O0007. 2.0 Commercial Solutions Opening with Calls This Commercial Solutions Opening is a hybrid solicitation against which both Closed Calls and/or Open Period Calls can be published via amendments to the Commercial Solutions Opening. All Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening will include specific instructions including dates, AoIs, evaluation criteria and proposal instructions to potential offerors. While each offeror shall adhere to this Commercial Solutions Opening, the Calls can contain other information the Contractor shall adhere to. Each Call will be announced on the Government Point of Entry (beta.SAM.gov), which may result in the award of a FAR Part 12, Procurement for experimental purposes under 10 U.S.C. 4023 contract or an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under 10 USC 4021. 2.1 Closed Calls (One-Step or Two-Step) Over the period of this Commercial Solutions Opening, Calls may be issued to request white papers and/or proposals for specific AoIs. It will be determined on a Call-by-Call basis whether or not the announcement is for a one-step (Proposals only) or a two-step process (White Papers first, then Proposals by invite-only). The submission for white papers and proposals shall be submitted at a specific date and time as set forth in each particular Call. White papers and/or proposals will not be reviewed if submitted after the stated date and time. No exceptions will be made for late proposal submission, including technology issues encountered during submission. One-Step Calls Step 1: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Calls issued against this Commercial Solutions Opening. Two-Step Calls Step 1: White Paper due date and time will be provided in Calls issued against this Commercial Solutions Opening Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Requests for Proposals (RFPs) sent to offerors that submit White Papers who are evaluated well in accordance with the criteria stated in each Call. 2.2 Open Period Calls (Two-Step) This Commercial Solutions Opening may also have Open Period Calls. Open Period Calls will only be issued under a two-step process. After an Open Call is published, white papers may be submitted at any time during an Open Period for the AoIs detailed in the Call. It is important to note that only white papers submitted in response to the specific AoIs detailed in the Call will be considered. Step 1: White paper submission period will be provided in Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening. Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Requests for Proposals (RFPs) sent to offerors that submit White Papers who are evaluated well in accordance with the criteria stated in each Call. 3.0 TECHNOLOGY FOCUS AREAS (TFAs) Each Technology Focus Area identifies an area where prospective Contractors can bring substantial value to meet the JADC2 mission. This Commercial Solutions Opening is not limited to the following TFAs. Additional TFAs may be included via amendments to this Commercial Solutions Opening. Digital Architecture, Standards and Concepts This category consists of various activities to analyze, mature, and document the foundational aspects of the development of the overall enterprise architecture. This includes digital modeling, simulation and analysis, trade studies, government owned standard development and maintenance, and potential concept development and refinement. Development of digital engineering architecture to include appropriate toolsets, licenses, data, etc., at multiple levels of security and including services such as data management, configuration control, and security/access management. Other activities may include architecting the toolchains to support the linkage of digital engineering artifacts to modeling and simulation tools and operational analysis. Sensor Integration The development, maturation, integration, demonstration, and proliferation of sensor hardware and software. title: Repair Punta Borinquen Lighthouse at USCG Base Borinquen, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico (PNUM 2993811)
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: THIS PROJECT IS BEING SET ASIDE FOR TOTAL HUBZONE BUSINESS CONCERNS. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT THIS SET ASIDE WILL BE SOLICITED VIA INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). THE SOURCES SOUGHT THAT WAS POSTED FOR THIS PROJECT IS AS FOLLOWS: PN 2993811 � REPAIR PUNTA BORINQUEN LIGHTHOUSE AT UNITED STATES COAST GUARD BASE BORINQUEN, AGUADILLA, PUERTO RICO. This is not a pre-solicitation notice or solicitation for proposals/quotations. The base bid, on-site work consists of furnishing all labor, tools, equipment, materials, supervision, and transportation necessary for, and incidental to, Repair Punta Borinquen Lighthouse. The following is a general summary of the work: Develop and provide asbestos containing material (ACM) and lead based paint (LBP) investigation and analysis report. Prep surface with a combination of high-pressure water and spot washing with a stiff brush and cleaning solution on 3,200 square feet (SF) of exterior surface at the Punta Borinquen Lighthouse. Prep surface with a combination of high-pressure water and spot washing with a stiff brush and cleaning solution, as well as strip LBP within interior walls and metal stairway (2,560 SF). Repair spalling damage on the exterior wall and overhang on Punta Borinquen Lighthouse. Apply minor repairs to 160 square feet damaged areas, cracks, and unsound surface of exterior surface by dry cutting and patching. Repair rust damage on roof level and replace one two-square feet metal hatch access to roof, as we; as install 45 linear feet of metal guardrails along the roof edge. Replace a five feet 10 inches wide and nine feet six inches high entrance metal door to match existing on the Punta Borinquen Lighthouse. Replace a two feet six inches by three feet three inches metal louver window on first level to match existing on the Punta Borinquen Lighthouse. Base coat and paint with two coats of algae-resistant water-based elastomeric, high-build, acrylic coating (6,000 square feet) on concrete surfaces. Treat all metal surfaces with rust converter and apply rust resistant paint. The performance period will be one hundred eighty (182) calendar days. The estimated value of this procurement is between $100,000 and $500,000. The applicable North American Industry Class System (NAICS) code is 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction). The small business size standard has an annual gross receipt of $45 million. Bid, Payment, and Performance Bonds are REQUIRED. The following are tentative dates for this project: Solicitation Issued: September 2026 Bid Opening: October 2026 Contract Performance Completion: May 2027 SAM: Interested parties should register in the System for Award Management (SAM) database as prescribed in FAR 4.203-1(b). SAM registration can be obtained by accessing the internet at www.sam.gov. USCG posts opportunity and award information to SAM. The U.S. Coast Guard is considering whether or not to set aside this acquisition for a HUBZone, Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Total Small Business or Women Owned Small Business (WOSB) concerns. In accordance with FAR 19.1303, FAR 19.1403, FAR 19.50, and FAR 19.1503 if your firm is HUBZone certified, Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Total Small Business or Women Owned Small Business (WOSB) and intends to submit an offer for this acquisition, please respond via email to Cherie.R.Rappaport@uscg.mil with �Sources Sought PN 2993811 � Repair Punta Borinquen Lighthouse at USCG Base Borinquen, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico� in the subject line. Please reference the above project number in all correspondence pertaining to this project. Your response MUST include the following: (a) a positive statement of intent to submit a bid/proposal for this solicitation as a prime contractor; (b) a statement identifying you are a certified small business designation; (c) evidence of experience with work similar in type and scope to include contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, points of contact, and telephone numbers; (d) evidence of bonding capability to the maximum magnitude of the project, to include both single and aggregate totals; (e) documentation verifying small business certification and socioeconomic category designation by SBA; (f) Unique Entity ID (UEI). Contractors are reminded that should this acquisition become a set aside concern, the following FAR Clauses may apply: FAR 52.219-3 Notice of Total HUBZone Set-Aside; FAR 52.219-6 Notice of Total Small Business Set-Aside FAR 52.219-28; Notice of Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside FAR 52.219-27; Notice of Women Owned Small Business Set-Aside FAR 52.219-30. Responses are required no later than September 11, 2026 at 4:00 PM EST. All information above MUST be submitted in sufficient detail for a decision to be made on which type of small business concern set aside to pursue. Disclaimer and Important Notes: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Failure to respond or submit information in sufficient detail may result in a company not being considered as a likely offeror when making a decision on whether or how to set aside a solicitation for restricted competition. Regardless of the information obtained from this Sources Sought Notice, the Government reserves the right to consider any arrangement as deemed appropriate for this requirement. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. At this time no solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. After a review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation notice and solicitation may be published on the SAM website (http://SAM.gov). It is the potential offeror's responsibility to monitor Contract Opportunities on the SAM website for release of any future solicitation that may result from this Sources Sought Notice. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will not be considered adequate responses to any resultant solicitation.

title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss nicht-exklusiver Rabattvereinbarungen nach § 130 a Abs. 8 SGB V ab dem 01.04.2026
description: § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen (KK) und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen KK abzugebenden Arzneimittel zu schließen. Die GWQ wird als Gesellschaft für Wirtschaftlichkeit und Qualität bei KK gem. § 130a Abs. 8 S. 5 SGBV für ihre Aktionärs- und Kundenkassen tätig. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die GWQ ServicePlus AG statt. Bis zum In Krafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge möchte die GWQ mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abschließen. Vertragsstart ist der 01.04.2026.

title: Lease of Office Space within Norfolk, VA. Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) #26NAT02
description: This advertisement is incorporated by reference into Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) #26NAT02 as an attachment. Sisäisiä kilpailutuksia voidaan tehdä DPS:n hankintavaiheen alettua. Hankintasopimukset tulee tehdä ennen dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän päättymistä. Luokka 2 Kalusteet palveluhankintana: Hankintasopimukseen perustuvia hankintoja (tilauksia) voidaan tehdä ennen hankintasopimuksen päättymistä. title: Netherlands – Health and social work services – BZK-EA Providerbogen Bedrijfszorg voor Bedrijfsartsen
description: Organisatie en Personeel Rijk|Bedrijfszorg (O&P Rijk) is op zoek naar bedrijfsartsen. Daartoe is een zogenaamde providerboog voor bedrijfsartsen opgericht. Een providerboog is een specifieke groep zorgvuldig geselecteerde professionals die voldoen aan bepaalde kwaliteitsnormen en ingehuurd kunnen worden tegen vooraf vastgestelde all-in tarieven. De providerboog staat doorlopend open voor aanmelding van nieuwe bedrijfsartsen. Het is voor iedere bedrijfsarts in Nederland die voldoet aan de criteria mogelijk om zich aan te melden. Als bedrijfsarts speel je een belangrijke rol op het gebied van duurzame inzetbaarheid van medewerkers en werk je volgens het door de Rijksoverheid gehanteerde ‘eigen regiemodel’. Bij dit model zijn functioneren, ontwikkeling, inzetbaarheid en gezondheid van de medewerker de gezamenlijke verantwoordelijkheid van medewerker en leidinggevende. De bedrijfsarts is adviseur van de leidinggevende en medewerker, niet de beslisser in het verzuimproces. De organisatie O&P Rijk is een nieuwe uitvoeringsorganisatie én de grootste HR-serviceverlener van de Rijksoverheid. O&P Rijk valt onder het Ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties. Voor alle medewerkers, managers, HR-directies en beleidsmakers van het Rijk bieden we basisdienstverlening en dienstverlening op maat. Met ruim 2000 medewerkers zet O&P Rijk zich in voor alle 140.000 rijksambtenaren. Met ruim 250 medewerkers geeft de business unit Bedrijfszorg advies over preventie, duurzame inzetbaarheid, vitaliteit, re-integratie, psychosociale hulpverlening en heel veel andere zaken op het terrein van arbeid, gezondheid en productiviteit. Met als doel gezonde, gemotiveerde en betrokken medewerkers en vitale organisaties waarin het zinvol en plezierig werken is. Partnerschap met al onze interne klanten staat hierbij centraal. De professionals van Bedrijfszorg werken niet alleen aan een het oplossen van individuele problemen, maar dragen ook bij aan gezondheid bevorderende organisatiekenmerken en het versterken van eigenaarschap van alle medewerkers.

title: Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) Netting Installation for Aircraft Sunshade Structures
description: Market Research Only � Not a Request for Proposal Title: Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) Netting Installation for Aircraft Sunshade Structures Notice Type: Sources Sought NAICS Code: 238990 � All Other Specialty Trade Contractors Response Due Date: 13 November 2026, 4:00 PM Local Time Submit Responses To: matthew.lahr.3@us.af.mil 1. Purpose The United States Air Force is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing all design, materials, labor, and equipment necessary to furnish and install counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) netting on existing aircraft sunshade structures. A primary purpose of this notice is to determine whether this requirement can be set aside for small businesses under the SBA guidelines for NAICS 238990. The Government is seeking to determine the availability and capability of small business concerns (including 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB) to perform this work. This notice is issued solely for market research and small business set-aside determination purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid, or any other form of solicitation. The Government does not guarantee that a contract will result from this notice, and the Government will not reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in preparing or submitting a response. The Government is also interested in unique and innovative solutions, including any proof-of-concept or operational C-UAS netting installations already fielded or under evaluation at other Department of Defense installations. 2. Requirement Overview The contractor shall design, furnish, and install counter-UAV netting on all four sides of six (6) existing aircraft sunshade structures. Each structure is approximately: Length: 630 feet Width: 65 feet Height: 30 feet Configuration: 6 bays per structure A drawing of the aircraft sunshade structures is attached to this notice. Primary Objective: Prevent Group 1 (�small�) Unmanned Aerial Vehicles from penetrating the interior of the sunshade structures to protect aircraft and personnel. 3. Technical Requirements (Minimum) The proposed netting system must meet or exceed the following: Material: UV-resistant, moisture-resistant, capable of withstanding temperatures up to 400�F. Polyester or Nylon are preferred. Tensile strength: 200 lbs or greater. Mesh opening: Netting squares no larger than 3 inches across. Performance: Capable of stopping Group 1 small UAVs from penetrating the structure without compromising the netting. Wind Load: Must meet Miami-Dade County Wind Load rating requirements. Retractability: Netting installed on the north- and south-facing sides shall be quickly and easily retractable to allow normal aircraft entry and exit. Engineering Support: The contractor shall utilize licensed professional engineers (as applicable). Structural engineers may be required to evaluate the load capacity of the existing metal sunshade structures and design appropriate attachment methods. The contractor is responsible for all design, material procurement, fabrication, installation, testing, and any structural modifications required for a complete and functional system. 4. Capabilities Package Requirements All interested parties (large and small businesses) are encouraged to submit a capabilities package limited to 10 pages total. The package must include, at a minimum: a. Company name, CAGE code, UEI number, business size status (including small business size standard under NAICS 238990), and socioeconomic category (if applicable). b. Relevant past performance on similar projects (large-scale netting, screening, protective systems, or specialized fabric installations on metal structures, preferably aviation-related). c. Technical approach or conceptual design solution addressing the material, performance, wind-load, retractability, and engineering requirements. d. Experience with structural engineering analysis and load calculations on existing metal structures. e. Description of any innovative or unique C-UAS netting solutions your company has developed or installed. f. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing and estimated period of performance (optional but highly desired). g. Any other information demonstrating your company�s ability to successfully perform this requirement. Small businesses are especially encouraged to respond and clearly identify their business size status. 5. Submission Instructions Email your capabilities package to: matthew.lahr.3@us.af.mil Subject Line: �C-UAS Sunshade Netting Sources Sought � [Company Name]� Deadline: No later than 13 November 2026, 4:00 PM Local Time 6. Disclaimer This Sources Sought notice is for information and planning purposes only. Responses will be used to assess industry interest and capability, and specifically to determine whether a small business set-aside is feasible. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice.

title: Bulgaria – Pharmaceutical products – Доставка на медикаменти за нуждите на МБАЛ "Свети Николай Чудотворец" ЕООД, гр. Лом
description: ДСП се създава за доставка на различни видове медикаменти за нуждите на МБАЛ "Свети Николай Чудотворец" ЕООД, гр. Лом. Първоначално планираната "Техническа спецификация" може да бъде частично променяна в хода на провеждане на динамичната система, като се добавят нови медикаменти и/или се променят количествата им. Посочените количества в приложената към документацията „Техническа спецификация“ са прогнозни и не пораждат задължение за Възложителя да ги възложи в прогнозния обем. Фактическото изпълнение на обществената поръчка ще се определи на базата на реално доставените медикаменти. Обменът на документи и съобщения между Възложители, кандидати, участници и изпълнители на обществени поръчки се осъществява чрез Централизираната електронна платформа. Срокът на ДСП е 36 месеца. Динамичната система за покупки е отворена през целия си срок на действие за всеки кандидат, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Достъпът и участието в нея са свободни и безплатни за всички заинтересовани лица. Срок на договорите, сключвани въз основа на ограничените поръчки в рамките на ДСП е за период до 12 /дванадесет/ месеца. Динамичната система за покупки (ДСП) се провежда на етапи. Съгласно чл.101 от ЗОП, в зависимост от етапа на процедурата кандидатите подават заявления за участие, а квалифицираните (допуснати) кандидати - оферти. ДСП се управлява като изцяло електронен процес и през целия срок на действие на системата за покупки тя е открита за всеки стопански субект /изпълняващ орган/ИО/, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Посочените критерии за подбор, са и критерии за изключване. Възложителят осигурява пълен, неограничен и пряк достъп до документацията по настоящата процедура чрез Централизираната електронна платформа, наричана "платформата". Заявленията и офертите трябва да се изготвят и представят в съответствие с изискванията на чл. 101 от ЗОП и чл.47 от ППЗОП, в срока посочен в обявлението. Всяко заявление и Всяка оферта се подава в системата на ЦАИС ЕОП. Първи етап /първоначално събиране на заявления за участие/: Квалифициране на доставчиците (допускане на доставчиците до системата). На този етап се събират заявления за участие. Заявленията за участие /ЕЕДОП/ съдържа/т информация относно личното състояние на кандидатите и критериите за подбор. Краен срок за подаване на първоначални заявления - 19.12.2024 г. Разглеждането на първоначалните заявления за участие ще се извърши в срок до 10 работни дни от крайният срок за подаване на първоначални заявления. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички първоначални заявления. Заявления могат да се подават и след крайния срок за подаване на първоначални заявления, в тези случаи кандидатите ще получават покани след одобряване на включването им в ДСП. Възложителят определя с Решение за подбор квалифицираните доставчици. След влизане в сила на Решението за подбор следва втори етап на процедурата. Втори етап /събиране на оферти по конкретни покани/: Следва изпращане на покана за представяне на оферти за конкретна обществена поръчка до тези доставчици, които са били квалифицирани/допуснати. Офертите съдържат техническо и ценово предложение. Съгласно чл.39, ал.1 от ППЗОП с подаването на оферта се счита, че кандидатите се съгласяват с всички условия на възложителя, в т.ч. с определения от него срок на валидност на офертите и с проекта на договор. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички първоначални заявления, подадени в посоченият по-горе срок. Осигурен е неограничен, пълен и пряк достъп до документацията за обществената поръчка през целия срок на действие на ДСП. *По всяко време заинтересовани лица могат да подават заявления за допускане/включване в ДСП. Възложителят ще разглежда новопостъпилите заявления два пъти в месеца /всеки понеделник от първата и третата седмица на месеца/. Възложителят ще издава решение за допускане на кандидатите в ДСП. След всяко разглеждане на заявленията Възложителят издава Решение за подбор с което квалифицираните доставчици се присъединяват към ДСП.

title: Slovakia – Cadastral surveying services – DNS_Geodetické služby
description: Predmetom zákazky je zriadenie dynamického nákupného systému a zadávanie jednotlivých zákaziek v rámci vyhláseného DNS na predmet zákazky s názvom: DNS_Geodetické služby. Predmetom zákaziek zadávaných v dynamickom nákupnom systéme (ďalej ako "DNS") sú: Vypracovanie geometrických plánov pre majetkovo - právne usporiadanie pozemkov a stavieb, rozčlenenie, oddelenie pozemkov a stavieb, na vecné bremená, vytyčovanie hraníc pozemkov, líniových stavieb, polohopisné a výškopisné zameranie pozemku, geodetické práce súvisiace s vytýčením stavieb a porealizačným zameraním stavieb, prešetrenie majetkovo - právnych vzťahov, vrátane ich zápisov do evidencie katastra nehnuteľností alebo pre ďalšie konanie orgánov štátnej správy a samosprávy, pre potreby súdnych sporov a iných konaní pre jednotlivé odštepné závody ako aj všetky ďalšie možné geodetické služby poskytované v zmysle zákona č. 162/1995 Z.z. o katastri nehnuteľností a o zápise vlastníckych a iných práv k nehnuteľnostiam (katastrálny zákon). Konkrétny rozsah predmetu zákazky ako aj jeho podrobná špecifikácia bude súčasťou jednotlivých výziev v rámci zriadeného DNS, ktoré budú zaslané všetkým kvalifikovaným záujemcom prostredníctvom systému JOSEPHINE.

title: Request for Information: Multi-Source PNT UE
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, respondents must describe their current capability to safeguard CUI/CDI. Please indicate your current compliance status with NIST SP 800-171, confirm whether an active assessment score exists within the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS), and state your current readiness posture for the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) (Level 2 or higher). c. title: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration at NSB Kings Bay, GA
description: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Request for Information (RFI) for Construction Project for building in the State of Georgia Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration at Naval Submarine Base (NSB) Kings Bay, GA This project will include, but is not limited to, renovate the Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing Quarters (Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 and 1054) located at Naval Submarine Base (SUBBASE), Kings Bay, Georgia. Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045 and 1046 were constructed in 1984. Building 1054 was constructed in 1989. The project scope includes upgrades to mechanical systems, fire protection, fire alarms, bathrooms, and exterior renovation. Except for Air Handling Units (AHU) in Buildings 1042, 1044 and 1046, all mechanical systems are being upgraded under this project. Mechanical system repairs include replacement of HVAC AHUs, installing Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for temperature and humidity, replacement of chilled water (CHW) piping, circulation pumps and cleaning of ductwork. Plumbing repairs include the replacement of plumbing fixtures, domestic water piping and sanitary piping. Electrical system repairs include replacement of electrical service panels throughout the building. Electrical repairs also include replacement of lighting fixtures with LED fixtures and replacement of wiring and wiring devices where they do not meet the current codes. Exterior renovation includes replacement of gutters, windows, doors, safety railings, lights. Interior renovation includes remodeling of bathrooms, mold remediation, and cleaning and painting of all previously painted surfaces. Ceilings and non-loadbearing walls will be demolished and rebuilt as required to allow access to rebuild mechanical and plumbing ductwork and pipes. The project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 236220. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25,000,000 - $50,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 1,200 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.502-2 (d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. This is not an announcement of the availability of a solicitation nor is it a means of generating a plan holder�s list. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Darrien Thomas at darrien.a.thomas.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00PM Eastern Standard Time on November 17, 2026.

PRESOLICITATION NOTICE FOR LAKE GEORGE EAST PHASE II DREDGING, EAST CHICAGO, LAKE COUNTY, ILLINOIS
description: This Pre-Solicitation Notice is being issued by the United States Army Corps of Engineers ? Chicago District to inform interested vendors of the district?s intent to issue a solicitation for Lake George East Phase II Dredging, East Chicago, Lake County, Illinois. PROJECT INFORMATION: The Lake George East Phase II Dredging project includes removal of contaminated sediments in the Lake George Canal (LGC) section of the Indiana Harbor Canal (IHC) via mechanical dredging with appropriate environmental monitoring and controls to improve sediment quality, water quality, and habitat within the LGC. Sediment within the LGC contains elevated concentrations of metals, volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds, and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) due to legacy contamination from adjacent and upstream sources. Dredged material will be hydraulically placed into the IHC confined disposal facility (CDF) adjacent to the LGC. The project may include sediment sampling at the dredged surface to determine if further remediation is required to achieve project remediation goals. Further remediation, if needed, will be performed under a separate project. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: Competition for this acquisition is RESTRICTED to SMALL BUSINESS CONCERNS. The North American Industry System Classification Code is 237990, with a small business size standard in dollars of $37 Million. The magnitude of cost for construction is estimated between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The requirement is for 545 calendar days: one (1) year and six (6) months. The solicitation package is planned for advertisement Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 and bids are planned to be opened in the Second Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026. The solicitation will be downloadable from the internet only. The project specification files are PDF files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. Once the package is released into advertisement at this website, interested bidders may download the full package, which includes- specification and drawing files. IMPORTANT POLICY: Contractors are REQUIRED to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) AT THE TIME ITS BID IS SUBMITTED to comply with the annual representations and certifications requirements. Registration can be completed free of charge at www.sam.gov. Contractors must register with sam.gov, prior to registering with the DoD Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) system. Your firm must register with PIEE in order to access the solicitation and to place a bid in response to the upcoming USACE Solicitation. Use the PIEE System Registration link: ? https://piee.eb.mil and follow the instructions on their website. Request for Solicitation packages made by telephone, fax, or e-mail will not be honored. The Point of Contract for this acquisition is Ericka Hillard at ericka.d.hillard@usace.army.mil. Please include Solicitation number W912P626BA015 on all correspondence.

description: This Pre-Solicitation Notice is being issued by the United States Army Corps of Engineers- Chicago District to inform interested vendors of the district?s intent to issue a solicitation for Upper Appleton Wall Repair, Appleton, Outagamie County, Wisconsin. PROJECT INFORMATION: The scope primarily includes removing the existing material on the upstream face of a stacked masonry stone wall, shotcrete, applying a waterproofing system, and replacing the material to the east and west of the Upper Appleton hydropower plant.
